subject: Arts Collaborative Medford
overview: Danielle Balocca interviewed Regina Parkinson, executive director of Arts Collaborative Medford, about the organization's new space on Mystic Avenue. Parkinson detailed their studio spaces, community programming, partnerships, and upcoming artist scholarship.

items.title: Introduction and Favorite Local Food
items.summary: Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan introduced the podcast, and guest Regina Parkinson discussed her background and named Deep Cuts as her favorite local restaurant.

items.title: Overview and Community Vision for Arts Collaborative Medford
items.summary: Parkinson shared that the collaborative opened its space at 162 Mystic Avenue in January, focusing on studio artists, gallery events, and expanding community programming across multiple creative disciplines.

items.title: Director Background and Operating Philosophy
items.summary: Parkinson recounted her background in art history, curation, and non-profit leadership, emphasizing an artist-first approach focused on local creative opportunities.

items.title: Artist Cohort and Institutional Partnerships
items.summary: Parkinson outlined the inaugural cohort of eight local artists and highlighted partnerships with Tufts University, the School of the Museum of Fine Arts, Event Them, and Theory Wellness.

items.title: Public Access, Louise Muster-Choate Scholarship, and Community Support
items.summary: Parkinson shared public gallery hours, announced an upcoming subsidized studio scholarship named for Louise Muster-Choate, and invited community contributions through donations, supplies, and small artwork consignments.
